what: The one held-out evaluation of the trained segmenters (dacl10k v1, v2a, v2b) and the classical engine, each at its profile (drishyam.agent.PROFILES, unchanged) and charged the cost table the dev comparison charged it, each held-out set scored once per model. Nothing was tuned on these numbers.
criterion: The dev comparison's criterion (results/dev/model_choice_dev.json), unchanged, on the held-out counterparts of its splits: recall at the 30 % cap on CODEBRIM eval200 (for dev100) and synth200 (for synth_dev), and false alarms at the 30 % cap on the clean set synth_clean (for the clean dev split). A is better than B on a set when the paired 95 % bootstrap CI of A's recall ratio to B lies wholly above 1, worse when wholly below; A harms against B on the clean set when the CI of its boxes-per-photo difference or of its difference in the share of photos with any box lies wholly above 0. The dev choice of v1 rested on v1 being the only model with no measurable loss against any other (where_each_loses), so that is what this checks.

cost_note: Each model is charged its own table, timed on this Mac (x86, 1 cv2 thread per worker): v2b results/local-macos-x86-dacl10k_v2b/micro.json (2026-10-19T19:28Z, 1-min load 10.64 at start, 14.52 at end), v2a results/local-macos-x86-dacl10k_v2a/micro.json (2026-10-19T16:27Z, 1-min load 7.93 at start, 7.81 at end), v1 results/local-macos-x86-dacl10k-retime/micro.json (2026-10-19T16:31Z, 1-min load 8.0 at start, 7.39 at end), the classical engine results/local-macos-x86/micro.json (2026-10-17T20:19Z, 1-min load 23.82 at start, none recorded at end). One look at 4000x3000 (warp, quality and segment:accurate, p50) costs 1326.8 ms on v2b's table, 526.5 on v2a's, 568.1 on v1's and 108.0 on the classical engine's. v2a re-timed in v2b's window (runs/v2a/micro/local-macos-x86-dacl10k_v2a/micro.json, load 14.08 to 11.22) costs 1304.5: per look v2b costs 0.87 to 1.04 times v2a in one window across the three timed sizes, against 2.10 to 2.52 between their own tables, so the ms gap between v2b and v2a below is the machine load at timing, not the model. v1 and v2a were timed in one window (0.97 to 1.10 per look). The classical table's high load overstates its ms, so the ONNX models' ratios to it understate their extra cost at equal load.

The runs are in the main checkout's ignored runs/model-eval/. So for v1 these are second scorings; v2a and v2b had never been scored on any held-out set (no other run under runs/ or a worktree carries these sets' sha256s with an ONNX segmenter).
